trip.why: is_memory_file() passes (path contains '.claude/projects/' and '/memory/' and ends .md and is not MEMORY.md), so the hook reads the file OFF DISK and runs check_schema. That real vault memory file has valid YAML frontmatter but no 'expires' key, and REQUIRED_FIELDS includes expires, so check_schema returns a 'Missing fields' warning which main() emits as additionalContext. Trigger is the FILE CONTENT at file_path, not the payload: the payload only selects which file is read. Chosen deliberately over a temp fixture so the probe needs no setup; 313 of the 844 files in that memory folder currently violate this schema (measured 2026-08-23), so the target is representative, not a lucky pick. If it ever goes silent the file was fixed, and the replacement target is any other missing-expires file in the same folder.
trip.observed: stdout: {"additionalContext": "[MEMORY SCHEMA] decision_autonomy_two_gates_reversibility_floor_detectability_expander.md: Missing fields: expires"}, exit code 0. One hook-activity record went to the redirected HOOK_ACTIVITY_LOG_PATH (decision=warn). I separately confirmed the multi-field branch by pointing the same stdin shape at a temp file carrying only 'title:' in its frontmatter: 'Missing fields: confidence, description, expires, last_verified, name, type', exit 0.

pass.why: Same memory-folder path shape, so the hook does NOT take its silent non-memory exit: it reads the file and runs the full schema check. This one carries all six required fields (name, description, type, expires, confidence, last_verified) with a valid type, valid confidence and a well-formed last_verified date, so check_schema returns no warnings. This is the discriminating benign case: it proves the hook is reading content rather than warning on every memory-folder write.
pass.observed: stdout was exactly {} with no additionalContext, exit code 0; the activity record was decision=ok. I also ran the non-memory path (file_path = Vault/log.md) and got {} with exit 0 via the is_memory_file early return, confirming the scope guard.

trip.why: Matches the BLOCKED_PATTERNS row 'git force-push' (git, optional global options, push, .*--force). Force-push is the one git operation the 2026-08-05 Wiktor ruling explicitly kept as a hard deny when normal push was demoted to a warning, so this row is the Gate-1 reversibility floor itself. The command survives strip_inert_contexts (no quoted body, no -m message, no heredoc), so the deny loop sees it verbatim.
trip.observed: stdout: hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision = "deny", reason "BASH SAFETY: Blocked 'git force-push'. Command: git push --force origin main...", exit code 0. A deny record went to the redirected GOVERNANCE_LOG_PATH with pattern=git force-push. No gate1_surface_degraded alarm appeared in the redirected GATE1_ALARM_LOG_PATH, so _irreversible_surface imported cleanly and the deny came from the canonical surface, not the frozen fallback snapshot.

pass.why: A read-only git invocation. It is deliberately a git command rather than an unrelated one, so it proves the guard discriminates within the git surface instead of denying anything containing 'git'. It matches no BLOCKED_PATTERNS row, no WARN_PATTERNS row, no curl-write predicate, and no Windows reserved redirect target.
pass.observed: No stdout, no stderr, exit code 0 (the allow-silently path). Nothing was appended to the redirected governance log.

trip.why: classify_subagent_output CHECK 1: len(message) < 5 returns check_1_empty. The tool-call escape hatch does not apply because it only engages when last_assistant_message is blank after strip(), and 'ok' is not; there is also no agent_transcript_path in the payload, and _final_turn_used_tool fails closed on a missing path. NOTE ON MECHANISM, do not read this as a mismatch: a SubagentStop hook blocks by printing {"decision": "block"} on stdout and exiting 0, NOT by exit code 2. If a classifier keys on exit code alone it will label this 'warn'; the semantic class is block, and the regression it guards against is the hook falling silent.
trip.observed: stdout: {"decision": "block", "reason": "Agent output is empty (2 chars). Produce a substantive response."}, exit code 0. A block record went to the redirected GOVERNANCE_LOG_PATH with check_failed=check_1_empty. I also ran CHECK 2 with last_assistant_message = "I cannot do that.": {"decision": "block", ...matched: 'i cannot'...}, exit 0.

pass.why: 36 chars, so CHECK 1 (len < 5) and CHECK 3 (len > 500) do not apply, and CHECK 2 does not fire because the message carries no refusal keyword. It is also the shape the 2026-06-02 overfire fix was written for: a short bulleted NEGATIVE finding. A hook that blocked this would be over-firing on valid work.
pass.observed: No stdout, exit code 0. A pass record went to the redirected GOVERNANCE_LOG_PATH with message_len=36.

waivers.reason: Not probeable through stdin, and its output envelope cannot discriminate a trip from a pass. Every fire decision comes from the age of five state files whose paths are computed from the hook's own location (.claude/hooks/_state/{lint,governance-mine,setup-audit,work-triage,telemetry-check}-cadence.json) with NO env override, so no stdin field can move it; the payload is used only to stamp a session id on the activity record. Worse for probe purposes, main() ALWAYS prints the SessionStart envelope and exits 0 whether or not any suggestion fired, so both a trip and a pass classify as 'warn' and a pass assertion of must_not deny/block would be satisfied by any input at all: a control that fires on everything. There is also no reachable benign input on this machine today, since two builders are permanently overdue. NOT a defect: I verified the cadence logic really fires by importing the module and calling each builder directly, which returned [SETUP-AUDIT CADENCE] (76 days) and [WORK-TRIAGE CADENCE: OVERDUE] (44 days) with the other four correctly empty, and by running the hook end to end on {"hook_event_name":"SessionStart","source":"startup"}, whose stdout carried both strings plus the KNOWN-DISPATCH-NAMES REGEN line at exit 0. A real gate for this hook needs a state-file precondition the runner writes, which means writing live vault state, so it is out of scope here.

The Stop registration has no deny, block or warn path in its code at all, by design. _handle_stop increments turns_since_memory_write in the state file and returns; the module docstring states 'Prints nothing, ever' for Stop, and the nudge text is only ever emitted by the SessionStart registration (a different control, batch 9). So the only classification a Stop probe can ever produce is 'silent', and an expect of deny/block/warn would be a knowingly false expectation. Its actual enforcement IS observable as a state side effect, and I verified it rather than assuming: with MEMORY_NUDGE_STATE_PATH redirected to a scratch file, two successive {"hook_event_name":"Stop"} payloads moved turns_since_memory_write 0 -> 1 -> 2 (exit 0, no stdout both times), and a third payload carrying stop_hook_active: true correctly left it at 2, so the Stop-chain double-count guard works. If this suite later grows a state-delta assertion type, this control belongs in it.
